node-1.label: Patient developed left ear pain, hearing loss, purulent and blood-stained discharge, and left facial palsy after ear syringing

node-2.label: A woman in her 70s presented with impacted cerumen in the right ear and underwent two attempts at bilateral irrigation by a practice nurse; immediately after syringing, she reported pain and hearing loss in the left ear and subsequently developed purulent and blood-stained discharge in that ear

node-3.label: ENT examination found severe otitis externa with inflammation of the external auditory canal precluding a view of the tympanic membrane; after removal of a wick, a small anteroinferior perforation of the tympanic membrane was visualized

node-4.label: Patient developed left facial palsy with lagophthalmos, good static tone of the mouth, but weak movement on smiling (House-Brackman V)

why.why: The temporal relationship to ear syringing, severe otitis externa, tympanic membrane perforation, facial palsy, and CT/audiometric/tympanometric evidence of middle ear involvement all converge on ear syringing injury/infection. Both expert analyses favor this diagnosis, and the refined traumatic perforation with secondary otitis media/mastoiditis hypothesis further supports it. Confidence is increased from 0.8 to 0.85, though lack of culture and facial nerve MRI prevents complete certainty.

Tympanometry confirming tympanic membrane perforation and middle ear dysfunction, together with CT evidence of middle ear/mastoid fluid, shows disease beyond the external auditory canal. Isolated otitis externa with facial palsy is therefore largely refuted, and confidence is decreased from 0.15 to 0.10.

CT and audiometry/tympanometry confirm middle ear involvement, and both experts note that primary otitis media cannot be fully excluded without discharge culture and facial nerve MRI. However, the clear temporal relationship to ear syringing and expert interpretation of the findings as secondary infection make primary otitis media less likely, so confidence remains at 0.35.

node-9.label: Audiometry confirms mixed hearing loss and tympanic membrane perforation

node-10.label: Traumatic tympanic membrane perforation with secondary otitis media/mastoiditis caused by ear syringing

why.why: Both expert analyses explicitly support traumatic tympanic membrane perforation with secondary otitis media/mastoiditis caused by ear syringing, and tympanometry further confirms tympanic membrane perforation with middle ear dysfunction, reinforcing the CT and audiometric findings. The immediate post-syringing onset, ENT-visible anteroinferior perforation, and absence of bone erosion make irrigation-induced trauma with secondary infection the leading mechanism. Confidence is raised from 0.8 to 0.85; missing discharge culture and facial nerve MRI leave a small residual possibility of primary otitis media.

node-11.label: Tympanometry confirms tympanic membrane perforation and middle ear dysfunction

node-12.label: Facial nerve palsy is due to inflammatory involvement of the facial nerve secondary to otitis media/mastoiditis

attrs.why: The patient's facial palsy (House-Brackman V) developed in the setting of severe otitis externa, tympanic membrane perforation, and CT-proven middle ear/mastoid fluid. Both the radiologist and laboratory expert interpret the facial palsy as inflammatory facial nerve involvement, which is consistent with secondary otitis media/mastoiditis. Confidence is 0.7 because facial nerve MRI and microbial culture are still missing, so primary otitis media cannot be completely excluded.
